Hunt & HackettPerimeter review, October 2026

Remote access is now the weakest edge of the estate

The office network is in good order and the routes around it are neglected. We recommend retiring the legacy gateway before year end.

Prepared for the board by the security team, 10 October 2026.

  1. The legacy gateway still accepts passwords alone

    It predates single sign-on and was left running for two suppliers.

  2. Patching is fast wherever it is automated

    The servers that lag are the ones still patched by hand.

  3. Backups have never been restored in a test

    Nobody can say how long a recovery would take.

Exposure fell everywhere except remote access

We compared what an outsider can reach today with what they could reach at the last review. Four of five categories shrank, and remote access grew, because two supplier connections were added to the old gateway in the summer.

$ scan --external --since 2026-04-04
vpn-legacy.example.net   443/tcp   password only        # added for two suppliers in July
portal.example.net       443/tcp   single sign-on
Gateway
The appliance that ends remote connections inside the network.
Broker
The service that checks the person and the device before any connection is made.

One supplier laptop is two steps from the file servers

The gateway places its users directly on the server network, so nothing stands between a supplier's laptop and the shared drives.

Supplier connections on the legacy gateway
SupplierAccountsStatus
Facilities contractor14Passwords only
Payroll provider3Moving in November

Recommendation

Retire the legacy gateway by 15 December

It is the only option that removes the appliance. Both suppliers have confirmed they can move.

Until the gateway is gone, a supplier's password is the perimeter.
